answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of trusting it. A new agent posts a refundable bond and settles its first jobs through a verifier that samples proofs of execution; payouts unlock only as bonded stake accrues, and any proven duplicate node forfeits the whole bond. Launching a thousand puppets costs a thousand bonds plus a thousand verification fees, all slashable at once, while an honest agent reclaims its stake on exit. Reputation becomes a plume of receipts, not a name. A saffron seal stamps each attested batch so forks cannot be replayed, and a jade ledger records each slash.
